newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA EXPORTS SEEN HELPED BY THAI AID-MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA EXPORTS SEEN HELPED BY THAI AID-MINISTER.

text.p: Aid to stabilise the currency of Thailand would benefit Australian exports to Asian markets, Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said in a statement.

The aid would result in a restoration of confidence in the Thai financial system, which would help maintain and strengthen demand for Australian farm exports from Thailand and neighbouring countries, he said.

Anderson's comments followed a statement issued by the Queensland sugarcane farmer organisation CANEGROWERS on Tuesdsay, criticising the Australian government's decision to lend US$1 billion to Thailand in a currency swap to help support the country's currency.

CANEGROWERS chairman Harry Bonanno said the Australian sugar industry would be greatly alarmed if Australian aid were used in Thai sugar infrastructure or assisted Thailand's sugar industry in competing with Australian sugar.

Stability in Thai financial markets and a stronger Thai currency would put Australian sugar exporters in a better competitive position than if they faced a flood of devalued Thai sugar exports, Anderson said in his Wednesday statement.
Australia's support for the Thai rescue package was an important step forward in the development of strong and enduring links with Asian trading partners, he said.
